analysis.title: Global Insights (October 2026)
key_insights: Raymond James favors US equities over international developed equities. Favorite US sectors are Info Tech, Industrials, and Consumer Discretionary.
Among international markets, RJ is Overweight Japan and EM Asia, Neutral LatAm, and Underweight the euro zone and the UK.
The S&P 500 is up 12.4% YTD, slightly below its record high set Oct. 6. Energy and Tech are the top US gainers YTD.
After a 25 bp hike in September, markets expect the Fed to hold at 3.75%-4.00% on Oct. 28.
Betting markets show ~92% odds of Democrats winning the House and ~67% for the Senate ahead of the midterms.
The US Dollar Index is up 3.5% YTD, near the midpoint of its ten-year range, boosted by hawkish Fed rhetoric.
MSCI Europe is up 5.6% YTD in USD terms and trails the S&P 500 by about 7%, including currency headwinds.
Euro zone CPI rose from 3.2% in August to 3.8% in September, the seventh straight month above the ECB's 2% target. Markets expect the ECB to hold at 2.5% on Oct. 29 after hikes in June and September.
The euro is down 4.6% YTD, partly on investor concerns about France's budget deficits.
MSCI Japan is up 18.3% YTD in USD terms on solid earnings growth and expected fiscal stimulus. Markets expect the BOJ to hold at 1.25% on Oct. 30.
The 10-year JGB yield peaked at 3.11% on Oct. 7 and remains near its highest level since 1996. The yen is flat YTD but near its lowest levels since 1986.
MSCI UK is up 10.4% YTD in USD terms. Markets price a ~97% likelihood of a BOE hike on Nov. 5 from 3.75%, where the rate has been since Dec. 2025.
China's composite PMI rose from 49.5 in August to 50.1 in September, the 18th straight month in the 49-51 range.
MSCI India is down 15.5% YTD in USD terms. Low inflation and robust GDP have been offset by currency weakness.
MSCI Taiwan is up 56.7% YTD in USD terms, with September exports up 61% YoY on chips and electronics.
MSCI LatAm is up 25.7% YTD in USD terms on Energy and currency tailwinds. Lula defeated Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil's Oct. 25 run-off.

Spotlight: the bond sell-off is global. Higher energy and food prices drove the repricing of rate outlooks, but monetary policy, fiscal dynamics and country factors are increasing dispersion across markets.
10-year Treasury yields peaked near 5.3%, the highest since 2002. Markets price more than three Fed hikes over 12 months while RJ expects one. RJ sees the 10-year moving to 4.50%-4.75% over 2027.
The FY26 US budget deficit reached a post-COVID high of nearly $2 trillion, and CBO projects it rising over the next decade.

France's 10-year yield topped 5% for the first time since 2002 and its spread to German bonds is the widest since the 2011/12 debt crisis. A fiscal watchdog warning was the catalyst, and RJ sees little political appetite to act before the April presidential election.
Japan's 10-year yield passed 3% for the first time since 1996 but remains the lowest in the G7. RJ says the path of least resistance may be higher yields as the BOJ normalizes.
Brazil and China are the only G20 countries with lower yields YTD. China's CPI has stayed at 1.3% or less in 2026 on manufacturing overcapacity and a property downturn.
RJ expects a gradual easing of geopolitical tensions and falling commodity prices to cool inflation and bring yields lower, though unevenly.

risk_factors: Fiscal deficits: the US deficit near $2 trillion and France's deficit projected at 5% of GDP in 2027 pressure sovereign bonds.
Inflation driven by higher energy and food prices could keep yields elevated.
Japanese yields may drift higher as the BOJ normalizes and the government pursues fiscal stimulus.
International bonds add currency risk for US-based investors.
Emerging market weakness: India's currency and China's property downturn.
charts_described: Bar chart of YTD change in 10-year government bond yields across G20 economies: most rose between 40 and 90 bps, with Brazil and China the exceptions.
geopolitical: Iran conflict: the pound followed a more bullish trajectory than the euro during it.
RJ expects a gradual easing of geopolitical tensions, with oil returning to prewar levels.
US midterm elections: betting markets point to Democrats winning the House (~92%) and Senate (~67%).
Brazil's Oct. 25 presidential run-off: Lula da Silva defeated Flavio Bolsonaro.
France's presidential election next April limits appetite to address the budget deficit.
